angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the radius and distance: 2 x 523,166.4 km at 19.776 pc = 0.354 mas. The measured limb-darkened diameter is 0.3848 mas (Boyajian et al. 2015, MNRAS 447, 846, CHARA in the H band, as the JMDC lists it), 9 percent larger; the sphere keeps the eclipse map's stellar radius so the planet's orbit and size, fitted in units of it, stay as published.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 50.567 +/- 0.016 mas (photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv): 1000/50.567 = 19.776 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: 0.752 solar radii (523,166.4 km at 695,700 km per solar radius), the stellar radius Lally et al. (2025, arXiv:2503.20895, Table 1) fix for their eclipse map of HD 189733b. A model-dependent value; the interferometric diameter above gives 0.818 solar radii at the Gaia distance.
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 189733 (pscomppars): spectral type K2 V, from Paredes et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..176P/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 189733 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.02 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 189733 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.46119, from Barstow et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017ApJ...834...50B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 189733 (pscomppars): age 1.4 Gyr, from Southworth 2010 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010MNRAS.408.1689S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 189733 (pscomppars): rotation period 11.95 d, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 189733 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3.5 km/s, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the map paper's radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json) and dimmed toward the limb by a law fitted to TESS transits, because no image of the photosphere exists (see investigations.json). A star's limb is not a sharp surface.
